newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea aims to cut '97 trade deficit to $14 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea aims to cut '97 trade deficit to $14 bln.

text.p: South Korea's trade ministry said on Monday it would aim to cut the customs-cleared trade deficit to $14 billion in 1997 from $20.38 billion in 1996.
"We will take measures to boost exports and cut imports. They will bring down the deficit by about $6.4 billion," a ministry statement said.
It said exports would rise to $142 billion won this year from $129.8 billion in 1996, while imports were seen increasing to $156 billion, up from $150.2 billion.
"Without such measures, the deficit was expected to be almost the same as last year's," the statement said.
It said the ministry will streamline trade procedures, while seeking to reduce excessive consumption, which contributed to import rises in 1996.
Ministry officials said the deficit ballooned in 1996 due to plunging international prices for the nation's major exports, including semiconductors.
The ministry said it would help strengthen overseas marketing by exporters and foster local producers of parts and semi-manufactured goods to reduce reliance on imports.
"We will promote energy conservation campaign as part of efforts to cut imports," the statement said.
